boards.title: Your First Weekend at Kenyon College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A conservative Friday-to-Sunday sequence for learning Kenyon’s campus rhythm through dining, study, art, recreation and nearby nature.

cards.title: Friday: Find the Campus Spine
cards.subtitle: Stop 1 · Walk Middle Path before dinner
cards.notes: Start at the College Gates and follow Middle Path through campus, noting the buildings and gathering areas you will use throughout the weekend.
cards.short_summary: Use Kenyon’s central footpath to build a mental map of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon describes Middle Path as a ten-foot-wide footpath and central artery running the length of campus, with key points of interest along it.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus footpath; conditions may be muddy or slippery in poor weather.

cards.title: Friday: Learn the Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: Stop 2 · Eat inside Peirce Hall
cards.notes: Enter through the glass-roofed atrium, scan the available stations and choose a seat in Great Hall, Thomas Hall or the Alumni Dining Room.
cards.short_summary: Get oriented to Kenyon’s primary campus dining destination.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon states that Peirce Hall contains a servery with multiple food stations and three large dining rooms: Great Hall, Thomas Hall and the Alumni Dining Room.
cards.access_notes: Dining access and serving periods depend on the current AVI dining schedule and the student's meal-plan or payment eligibility.

cards.title: Friday: See the Sing Steps
cards.subtitle: Stop 3 · Pause outside Rosse Hall
cards.notes: Walk to Rosse Hall’s front steps and identify the setting for First-Year Sing; enter only when a scheduled public or campus event permits.
cards.short_summary: Connect a prominent performance hall with a documented first-year tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon identifies Rosse Hall as a 600-seat concert and lecture hall and documents its front steps as the site of First-Year Sing after Opening Convocation.
cards.access_notes: The exterior steps can be viewed from campus paths; auditorium entry depends on scheduled programming and building access.

cards.title: Saturday: Set Up a Study Base
cards.subtitle: Stop 4 · Explore Chalmers Library
cards.notes: Check the live daily schedule before entering, then locate circulation, technology help and the study-space reservation resources you may need later.
cards.short_summary: Learn where research help, technology support and study spaces converge.
cards.evidence_claim: The official library site identifies Chalmers Library as Kenyon’s library and publishes live building, circulation, archives and technology-center service hours.
cards.access_notes: Consult the official live schedule on the day of the visit; building and service-desk hours differ and may change between terms.

cards.title: Saturday: Make an Art Stop
cards.subtitle: Stop 5 · Visit The Gund’s exhibitions
cards.notes: Choose one current exhibition or collection display to examine closely, and confirm the day’s opening window on The Gund’s visit page first.
cards.short_summary: Add a free contemporary-art visit to the middle of Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: The Gund states that its Gambier museum welcomes all visitors to its collection, temporary exhibitions and public programs with free admission all year.
cards.source_title: Visit The Gund | All Welcome. Always Free.
cards.access_notes: Use the current hours posted on the official visit page; the museum is at 101½ College Drive between Cromwell Cottage and Chalmers Library.

cards.title: Saturday: Browse the Village Hub
cards.subtitle: Stop 6 · Step into the Bookstore
cards.notes: Browse the shelves and notice how the shop anchors the village center; confirm current opening hours before making it a fixed part of your route.
cards.short_summary: See the literary gathering place at the seam between campus and village.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon’s official virtual tour identifies the Bookstore as a gathering space in the heart of the village and an important hub of Kenyon’s literary scene.
cards.source_title: Kenyon on a Tour | Kenyon College
cards.access_notes: Retail hours are not stated on the cited tour page; verify current hours before visiting. Browsing does not obligate a purchase.

cards.title: Saturday: Sample Campus Recreation
cards.subtitle: Stop 7 · Tour the Lowry Center
cards.notes: Walk through the student-accessible areas and identify one recreation option for a later visit, following posted rules for each specialized facility.
cards.short_summary: Learn the layout of Kenyon’s large indoor recreation complex.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon describes the Lowry Center as a 265,000-square-foot facility with a pool, indoor track, courts, fitness spaces, study lounges and a movie theater.
cards.access_notes: Entry, equipment use and individual facility availability are governed by current Lowry Center membership, access and operating policies.

cards.title: Sunday: Follow the Trail Access
cards.subtitle: Stop 8 · Walk from Kenyon’s trailhead
cards.notes: Begin at Kenyon’s access point behind the athletic center and take a short out-and-back walk, turning around well before fatigue or changing weather.
cards.short_summary: Move from the Hill into the Kokosing River landscape on a defined route.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon identifies the area behind its athletic center as the College’s main access point to the Kokosing Gap Trail, which the community uses for exercise and leisure.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor multi-use trail; remain on the established route, account for the return distance and adjust plans for weather and daylight.

cards.title: Sunday: Walk a Preserve Trail
cards.subtitle: Stop 9 · Explore the BFEC in daylight
cards.notes: Select a trail from the official guide, carry water and stay on marked paths; choose a shorter option if the ground is wet or daylight is limited.
cards.short_summary: Experience prairie, woodland and river-valley habitats near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon describes the BFEC as a 700-acre preserve with more than ten miles of trails, open to the public seven days a week during daylight hours.
cards.source_title: Brown Family Environmental Center | Kenyon College
cards.access_notes: Open to the public during daylight hours. Follow official trail guidance and avoid wetland areas where access is restricted.

cards.title: Sunday: Close with the Music Wing
cards.subtitle: Stop 10 · Locate Storer Hall’s venues
cards.notes: Finish beside Rosse Hall by locating Storer’s recital and rehearsal spaces, then check Kenyon’s events listings for a future public performance.
cards.short_summary: End the route by identifying where campus ensembles rehearse and perform.
cards.evidence_claim: Kenyon identifies Storer Hall as the music department’s home, with a large ensemble rehearsal room and a 130-seat recital hall attached to Rosse Hall.
cards.access_notes: Interior access depends on building rules, classes, rehearsals and scheduled events; consult the College calendar before entering performance spaces.

warnings: Live hours, term schedules, meal access and recreation-facility eligibility should be reconfirmed immediately before the weekend.
